observation.visible_scene: A night waterfront scene: a low city skyline strung with warm lights stretches across the horizon above a calm dark body of water, whose surface carries vertical streak reflections of those lights. Several fireworks bursts occupy the sky above the skyline, with drifting pink smoke. The camera viewpoint and skyline position remain fixed across all frames.
visible_changes: A high oval/ring-shaped burst of white, red and blue dots sits center-upper in the sky, enveloped in pink smoke; it stays at the same screen position throughout the excerpt while its dots dim and the smoke spreads, fading to near-invisibility by the late frames.

A second, roughly spherical burst of dots appears to the lower-left of the oval (first faint around the 5th frame, orange then shifting to purple/pink), expands slightly, then gradually dims and breaks into scattered dots toward the end.

A third, low burst near the horizon line (pink/white) becomes clearly visible around the 14th frame, brightens, and persists to the last frame; its red light casts a vertical reflection column on the water below it.
Two small isolated white dots remain high in the sky (above the fading oval) from the mid-clip onward, staying at nearly fixed positions.

The city-light reflections on the water and the skyline itself do not change position, indicating no camera pan/zoom; only the firework lights and their water reflections vary in brightness and color.
outside_clip_unknowns: The launch points, fuses, or causes of each burst are not shown; the clip begins with the oval burst already expanded and ends before all bursts have fully extinguished.
Whether the two high white dots are falling embers, a separate distant burst, or a star/aircraft cannot be determined from this excerpt.
uncertain_details: Exact color identities of the fading dots (red vs pink vs white) shift with exposure and are approximate.
The relationship between the low horizon burst and the red water reflection is inferred as reflection, not a separate object, but the source geometry is not directly visible.
